---
title: "Colloquium, feedback and evaluation"
description: "Material for W8: the presentation brief, the critical perspectives, feedback cards and change requests, the transfer question and the anonymous course evaluation."
---

## Presentation brief (units 29 and 30)

Each group has **ten minutes** to present and **four minutes** for questions. Use at most six slides or one printed
page per section.

| Minutes | Content | The audience should be able to say afterwards … |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | The decision and the people affected | … what decision this is about and for whom. |
| 3 | Data, unit, baseline and validation, with one figure | … what was compared on which independent test data. |
| 2 | Uncertainty, errors by group and the counter-check | … how sure the result is and who carries the errors. |
| 2 | Ethics, regulation, data protection and security | … what the decision depends on beyond the numbers. |
| 2 | Recommendation, conditions, stop condition and next step | … what should happen now and when it will be reviewed. |

## Critical perspectives

Before unit 29 the course team draws which group holds which perspective for each presentation. Every project is
questioned from at least four perspectives.

| Perspective | Typical first question |
|---|---|
| Clinical use | "What does the team do differently on Monday morning, and what if the tool is down?" |
| Patients | "Who carries the errors, and how would they find out?" |
| Methods | "Which number would change most if the test set came from another hospital or species?" |
| Regulation | "Which sentence in your intended purpose decides the regulatory question?" |
| Data protection | "Which data leave the protected environment, to whom, and when are they deleted?" |
| Information security | "How would you notice that the model running is not the one you validated?" |

## Feedback card

One card per question asked. The presenting group receives all cards after the session.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Project and perspective | |
| Question asked | |
| Answer given (short) | |
| Was the answer supported by the passport or the decision sheet? (yes / partly / no) | |
| **Change request** (one concrete change, or "none") | |

## Comparing wrong decisions (unit 30)

After all six presentations, compare the projects in one table: what happens if the recommendation is wrong?

| Project | Wrong in which direction? | Who is harmed, how soon, how reversibly? | How would anyone notice? | Override or stop condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | |

## Revision note (unit 32)

A peer from another group checks your revised recommendation and its evidence.

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Change requests received | |
| What we changed and why | |
| What we did not change and why | |
| Evidence for the revised recommendation (passport row, figure or script output) | |
| Peer's check: is the revision supported? (yes / partly / no, with one sentence) | |

## Transfer question (unit 32)

Choose a research or care problem from your own work or studies and answer in at most half a page:

1. Which decision would data support, and who would act differently?
2. What is the independent unit, and which comparison would you need?
3. Which of the four perspectives (ethics, regulation, data protection, security) is most critical, and why?
4. What is the first step you could take in the next four weeks?

## Anonymous course evaluation

The evaluation is anonymous and separate from all assessment. It is collected on paper or with a form that stores
no names, and the course team reports only aggregated results.

**A. Self-assessment (same statements as in W1; 1 = not at all, 5 = fully)**

1. I can tell which number is the denominator of a percentage in a clinical study.
2. I can explain why images from the same patient in training and test data are a problem.
3. I can check whether a cited source actually supports a sentence.
4. I know who has to be informed, and by when, if patient data reach the wrong recipient.

**B. Course (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)**

5. The workshops built on each other in a way I could follow.
6. The required readings prepared me for the workshops.
7. The R labs were manageable with the help available.
8. The project helped me to connect the four parts.
9. The workload matched the stated hours.

**C. Technology**

10. Did technical problems (installation, packages, rendering) cost you time? (no / up to 1 hour / more than
    1 hour) What would have helped?

**D. Open feedback**

11. What should stay as it is?
12. What should change first?

The course team compares the anonymous answers to the two short cases from W1 and W8 together with this
evaluation to revise the course. A difference between before and after does not show that the course caused it;
that would need a suitable study design.

## Further reading

- [B28 · Case atlas, glossary and transfer](https://r-heller.github.io/clinical-data-science-in-r/chapters/b28-case-atlas-glossary.html#sec-b28-core)
  – six project cases and a navigator for new problems.
- Laupichler MC, Aster A, Haverkamp N, Raupach T. Development of the "Scale for the assessment of non-experts' AI
  literacy" – an exploratory factor analysis. *Computers in Human Behavior Reports*. 2023;12:100338.
  [doi:10.1016/j.chbr.2023.100338](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbr.2023.100338)
  – a published scale (SNAIL) that could complement the evaluation once language version and permission to use
  are clarified.
